Responsibilities:

You support the development, optimization and management of technical products and solutions.

You apply standards, guidelines and certification requirements, and support approval processes.

You work closely with customers and translate their needs into technical solutions.

You create and modify technical designs in CAD and manage the associated product data.

You collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Production and Quality to address technical questions and challenges.
 

Required qualifications:   

 
•  
Master's degree in Electromechanics, supplemented with initial work experience.

Practical knowledge of 3D CAD and MS Office.

Strong motivation and willingness to deepen your knowledge of standards, regulations and certifications.

• Involved in the (bio)-pharmaceutical drug development process of our clients. 

• Responsible for the development of complex LC-MS/MS methods for small molecules, proteins and/or oligonucleotides.  

• Operate & maintain LC-MS/MS and HRMS instrumentation, incl. routine performance checks, calibration and (basic) troubleshooting. You act as a subject matter expert on Mass Spectrometry. 

• Support the introduction, qualification and transfer of new MS technologies and analytical workflows. 

• Support lab operations in full compliance with GMP and data integrity standards.  

• You deliver data and reports according to high scientific and quality standards and interact with our clients to discuss scientific aspects. 
  
 

• PhD (or Master equivalent by experience) in a scientific field with a strong (technical) focus on mass spectrometry. 

• Extensive hands-on experience with LC-MS operation and troubleshooting on high resolution mass spectrometry platforms (ideally combined triple quad MS platforms) is essential. 

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work on complex analytical investigations, using a systematic root-cause approach to distinguish LC-, MS-, sample- and method-related issues.  

• Experience with a variety of chromatographic separations (e.g. RP-LC, HILIC) and/or nanoflow liquid chromatography is an additional asset. 

• Capable of working to the highest quality standards required to support development, qualification and validation of LC-MS based methods. 

• Proven ability to work in a dynamic laboratory environment to project timelines.  

• Excellent organization and communication skills in English. Knowledge of Dutch is an asset.

We are currently looking for a CQV Engineer to join one of our clients, a major player in the pharmaceutical industry, for a mission based in Belgium.

Your Profile 

• Degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field
• Proven experience in CQV within the pharmaceutical or biotech industry

• Fluent in English; French and/or Dutch is a plus
• Rigorous, autonomous, and comfortable working in a cross-functional environment
• Strong communication and documentation skills 
• The opportunity to work on high-impact projects with a major player in the pharmaceutical industry
• A career partner that adapts to your goals, your pace and your professional project
• A team of passionate consultants dedicated to the health industry

What if the algorithms you build don’t just run in simulation, but actually 
see, understand, and navigate the real world?
 

At M-ECS, you’ll turn perception algorithms into robust, real-time systems that help make off-highway vehicles and other robotic platforms autonomous. You’ll work at the intersection of computer vision, robotics and embedded systems, helping machines understand their surroundings and operate autonomously in demanding industrial and heavy-field environments.You’ll be part of the team shaping the next generation of autonomous machines, turning bold ideas into technology that works in the field.
 

You’ll see your work move from 
algorithm → machine → real-world impact.
 

YOUR ROLE, YOUR IMPACT.
 

As a hands-on Computer Vision & Perception Engineer, you’ll help build the perception capabilities that enable autonomous machines to operate safely and reliably in demanding real-world environments, from off-highway vehicles to other robotic platforms.
 

Key responsibilities:
 
 

• Developing perception capabilities for object detection, classification, multi-object tracking, depth estimation, and 3D reconstructions. 

• Processing and fusing sensor data from cameras, LiDAR, radar and GNSS/IMU systems to create reliable, real-time machine awareness. 

• Contributing to SLAM and localization systems that help machines understand where they are and where they’re going. 

• Optimizing algorithms for real-time execution on embedded and GPU platforms. 

• Bringing algorithms to life by integrating perception into machine control and navigation systems. 

• Testing and validating your work on real machines together with System Engineers. 

• Debugging and optimizing perception systems during field testing. 

ARE YOU THE ONE?
 

We’re looking for an 
all-round engineer who enjoys solving complex problems that don’t always come with a manual. You’re hands-on, curious and eager to turn ideas into working systems. You’re not afraid to figure things out along the way and shift gears when needed. You thrive in a fast-paced, ambitious tech scale-up, enjoy working as part of a team and take ownership of delivering high-quality results. 
 
 

• A 
 master’s degree in Automation, Robotics, AI, Computer Vision, or a related field. 

• 2–5 years of relevant experience, ideally in industrial automation, robotics or mobile machinery or equivalent hands-on experience. 

• Strong programming skills in 
Python and/or 
C++. 

• Hands-on experience with 
computer vision and deep learning for 
perception, including OpenCV, YOLO, or similar frameworks. 

• Solid understanding of 
sensor fusion, 
3D geometry, and 
coordinate transformations. 

• Knowledge of 
robotics and 
autonomous systems. 

• The ability to debug real-world systems, not just offline datasets. 

• Experience with ROS/ROS2, LiDAR, SLAM, edge platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson, embedded optimization, or dataset pipelines is a plus. 

• Strong communication skills in 
English and 
Dutch.

What if the systems you engineer don’t just work on paper, but actually power, control, and bring real machines to life? At M-ECS, you’ll design and integrate the electrical and automation systems that make off-highway vehicles and other robotic platforms work as one. You’ll work at the intersection of electrical engineering, automation, embedded systems, and system integration, helping machines operate reliably in demanding industrial and heavy-field environments.You’ll see your work move from
 idea → concept → system → real-world impact. 
YOUR ROLE, YOUR IMPACT. As a hands-on 
System Engineer, with a strong focus on
 Electrical & Automation Engineering, you’ll help design, integrate, test, and optimize the systems that make complex machines work in the field.You’ll connect the dots across electrical, automation, software, hydraulics, and mechanical systems, turning individual components and subsystems into one reliable, functional machine.
Key responsibilities: 
 
 

• Concept & Solution Engineering: Work directly with customers to understand their needs and challenges, challenge requirements where needed, and (co-)create technical solutions and system architectures that best addresses the problem. 

• Electrical Engineering: Design and integrate electrical architectures, components, wiring, sensors, actuators, and communication systems for off-highway vehicles and other machines. 

• Software, Automation & Controls: Program machine functions and control logic using PLCs, ECUs, and embedded systems. Integrate and commission control systems. 

• System Engineering: Connect electrical, software, hydraulic, and mechanical systems into a coherent and reliable machine architecture. Turn designs and ideas into functioning systems. 

• Testing & Commissioning: Build, integrate, commission, test, debug, and fine-tune prototypes and machines, turning concepts into reliable real-world solutions. 

• Customer Support, Training & Continuous Improvement: Support customers in the field or remotely, troubleshoot technical issues, provide hands-on training, and use customer and field feedback to continuously improve machine performance and reliability. 

ARE YOU THE ONE? You’re a
 hands-on Electrical Automation Engineer who enjoys understanding how things work, creating new solutions, and finding ways to make systems work even better. You don’t stop at the drawing board. You enjoy building, programming, testing, debugging, and improving real machines and you’re curious about what happens when your engineering meets the real world. You like digging into complex problems and don’t stop until you’ve turned your understanding into a practical and efficient solution, especially when there’s no obvious answer or manual to follow.
You approach challenges from a systems perspective, combining analytical thinking, creativity, and practical problem-solving. You’re curious, eager to learn, adaptable, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team. Most importantly, you thrive in a fast-paced and ambitious environment where you can tackle complex technical challenges and see your solutions work reliably in the field.
 
 

• A 
master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation, Electromechanics, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related field. 

• Approximately 
3–5 years of relevant experience in a similar engineering role, working with electrical systems, automation, controls, or embedded systems. 

• A strong interest in (off-highway vehicles), robotics, or intelligent machines. 

• Knowledge of 
PLC programming, preferably with CODESYS (Structured Text). 

• Knowledge of
 CAN-bus and/or other communication systems. 

• Strong knowledge of 
Eplan and electrical design. 

• Strong communication skills in 
Dutch and 
English. 

• Driver’s license B and a 
willingness to travel occasionally, both in Belgium and abroad.

You'll shape the structure, governance, and strategic roadmap of data assets across the organization¿ensuring data is accessible, secure, integrated, and aligned with evolving business needs.

You'll collaborate with senior stakeholders in IT, analytics, and the business to architect scalable data solutions across cloud, on-prem, and hybrid environments¿balancing innovation with long-term sustainability.

 

Key Responsibilities:

• Design and evolve enterprise data architecture, aligning with business strategies and regulatory requirements.
• Lead data modelling efforts across operational and analytical domains (OLTP/OLAP), including conceptual, logical, and physical models.

• Define and implement data standards, policies, and governance frameworks.

• Partner with Data Engineers, Analysts, Architects, and Business stakeholders to ensure data quality, accessibility, and lineage.

• Ensure data architecture enables AI/ML, advanced analytics, and reporting initiatives.
• Support compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, or other regulatory standards depending on the region/industry.
• Provide architectural oversight and leadership across data-related projects and programs.
• Mentor junior data architects and engineers, contributing to a strong data architecture community.

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or related field.
